findings.explanation: Splunkbase 4856 is 'Metrics Add-on for Infrastructure' (TA-linux-metrics), a Linux OS metrics add-on, not an NSX add-on. VMware's NSX-T Splunk App is Splunkbase 4241, and no Splunk_TA_vmware-nsxt package has been found on Splunkbase. The same wrong ID appears in dataSources, implementation, detailedImplementation and references.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 4856 with the real NSX integration (VMware NSX-T Splunk App, Splunkbase 4241, or whatever NSX add-on is actually deployed). Correct the package name and the sourcetypes it emits, and fix every field that repeats the wrong ID.

findings.explanation: None of these three syslog tokens appears in NSX's documented alarm catalogue. NSX's MTU alarm is 'MTU Mismatch Within Transport Zone', raised as an alarm, not as a syslog marker. The NSX Manager tunnels API reports tunnel and BFD state, but per-TEP-pair packet-loss, RTT and jitter fields from a /tunnels/{id}/stats route are not documented. The whole detection may rest on telemetry that does not exist.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the NSX 4.x alarm catalogue and API reference for the exact events and endpoints that expose TEP-to-TEP latency or loss (for example NSX latency monitoring features) and rewrite dataSources around them. If the metrics come only from a custom probe, say that explicitly.

findings.explanation: netcpa was the legacy control-plane agent and was replaced by nsx-proxy in later NSX-T releases. The other nsxdp-cli and nsxcli subcommands and the 'Path Health' UI blade are not supported by any grounding document and look invented. Following these steps would likely fail.
findings.quote: **`nsxdp-cli netcpa stats get`**, **`nsxdp-cli geneve get`**, **`nsxdp-cli vlanstats overlay-pnic-rx-drop`** ... **`nsxcli -c "get logical-overlay-tunnel <tunnel-id> stats"`** ... (System ▸ Fabric ▸ Hosts ▸ `<host>` ▸ Tunnels ▸ Path Health)
findings.suggested_fix: Check each CLI command against the NSX 4.x command reference and the UI path against the current NSX Manager. Remove anything that does not exist.

findings.explanation: VMware's MTU guidance gives 1600 bytes as the minimum and 1700 as the recommended value, so 1700 is not the minimum. With a 9000-byte underlay, VMware recommends a VM MTU of up to about 8800, at least 100 bytes (200 preferred) below the fabric MTU. The guidance contains no '8950' figure.
findings.quote: relax when fabrics advertise **`8950`** effective envelopes minus roughly fifty-byte GENEVE overhead (9000 minus 50 aligns with **`8950`** guidance cited beside VMware MTU references linked below) ... aligning with **`1700`** minimum envelopes
findings.suggested_fix: Quote VMware accurately: 1600 minimum and 1700 recommended overlay MTU, and VM MTU at least 100–200 bytes below the fabric MTU (about 8800 on a 9000 fabric). Explain the 400-byte gap in the MTU rule in those terms.

findings.explanation: The detailedImplementation copy of the search uses `sort()`, which is not an eval function, so the search fails when pasted. The spl field uses `mvsort()` instead. The text claims to paste the spl field, but the two copies differ.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the detailedImplementation search identical to the spl field, using mvsort().

findings.explanation: detailedImplementation points to knownFalsePositives entries (probe_interval_sampling_artefact, lag_rebalance_window, probe_cpu_saturation, tep_pool_exhaustion_onboarding) that do not exist there. The actual knownFalsePositives text is a generic maintenance/batch/probe template. detailedImplementation also uses fields the SPL never produces (tep_pool_used_percent, tor_maintenance_window, rack_id, site_code).
findings.quote: independent from **`probe_interval_sampling_artefact`** chatter summarized inside knownFalsePositives ... aligning with **`lag_rebalance_window`** commentary inside **`knownFalsePositives`**
findings.suggested_fix: Either write those named false-positive scenarios into knownFalsePositives with real causes (ToR maintenance, LAG rebalancing, CPU-starved ESXi hosts skewing probes, probe-interval artefacts) or remove the cross-references. Also remove or define the fields the SPL does not produce.

findings.explanation: Much of the text is dense, jargon-stacked prose that never says plainly what to configure or when to alert. It is full of em-dash asides and sibling-UC disclaimers, and a reader cannot pull an actionable runbook out of it.
findings.quote: those splits isolate overlay-quality regressions requiring probe—not failover—responses coordinated across networking plus virtualization crews referencing UC-18.2.5 narratives centered on binary posture rather than gradients tracked here.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite as short imperative steps: what to collect, which thresholds to alert on (loss ≥0.1%, jitter ≥1 ms, RTT ≥50 ms, MTU gap), and how to validate. Move sibling-UC boundaries to exclusions.

findings.explanation: Network_Traffic models flow and session records (src/dest, bytes, action). Probe-derived loss, RTT and jitter per TEP pair are not traffic records, and aliasing TEP IPs into it would pollute flow analytics. The SPL also never uses a datamodel.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop Network_Traffic. Keep Performance only if the metrics are actually mapped into it, or leave cimModels empty with a note that the telemetry is custom.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified by an automated agent reviewer, yet it contains a wrong Splunkbase ID and unverifiable NSX telemetry claims.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade status until an NSX SME has validated the data sources and commands.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The SPL depends on the custom sourcetype vmware:nsxt:tn_diag and on syslog tokens (OVERLAY_PATH_DEGRADED, MTU_MISMATCH, TUNNEL_PERFORMANCE_LOW) that NSX has not been shown to emit. The 'transport_node_overlay_context' branch flags any transport_node event mentioning 'tunnel stats', which will flood results without indicating any fault.
The title is an overlong keyword list and includes a sibling-UC reference ('Beyond Binary UP/DOWN UC-18.2.5').

summary: The UC rests on a wrong Splunkbase ID: 4856 is the Metrics Add-on for Infrastructure, not an NSX add-on. It also describes NSX syslog markers, per-TEP-pair loss/RTT/jitter API fields, CLI commands and UI paths that appear to be invented. The detailed implementation is dense word salad that cites false-positive labels which do not exist, and its MTU guidance misquotes VMware.
